item.title: Jesus Benavente: NUESTROWORLD
item.description:
Thursday, August 13, 2026 at 12 AM

Location: DiverseWorks, @ 5601 B Navigation Blvd & Various Locations, 5601 B Navigation Blvd, Houston, TX, 77011, United States

Opening Thursday, August 13, 2026 | 6 – 8 pm DiverseWorks @ 5601 B Navigation Blvd NUESTROWORLD is a satirical solo installation by Brooklyn-based artist Jesus Benavente. Featuring newly commissioned works, NuestroWorld opens on Thursday, August 13, 2026, transforming 5601 B Navigation Blvd, Houston, TX 77011 into a fictional visitor center for NuestroWorld, encouraging guests to explore Houston beyond the gallery walls and experience the city as an amusement park. The installation will be on view through September 13, 2026, with a closing party on September 11. Gallery hours are Thursday – Saturday, 12 – 6 pm. Admission is free. Through satire and spectacle, NuestroWorld examines how cities construct identity through tourism, branding, memory, and myth, inviting audiences to reconsider Houston’s past and present. The exhibition draws inspiration from pivotal moments in Houston and Texas history, including the opening of the Astrodome and Astroworld in the late 1960s, Selena’s iconic Houston Livestock Show & Rodeo performances in the 1990s, and the folklore surrounding Santa Anna’s capture following the Battle of San Jacinto in 1836, highlighting the city’s recurring cycles of ambition, folly, and heartbreak. The title plays on “Astroworld” and uses Spanglish to create the phrase “The World Is Ours,” reframing Houston’s cultural mythology through humor, nostalgia, and critical reflection. Opening Reception Thursday, August 13, 6 – 8 pm Artist and Curator Talk: 6:45 pm Closing Party Friday, September 11, 2026, 6 – 8 pm 7 pm: special performance by CTS Trio – Queen of Tejano & Latin Tribute ARTIST BIO: Jesus Benavente is a visual artist based in Brooklyn, New York, and born in San Antonio, Texas. Benavente earned an MFA from Rutgers University and attended Skowhegan School of Painting and Sculpture. Recent exhibitions and performances include Reception Rome, Italy; the Whitney Museum of American Art, New York; Queens Museum; LTD Los Angeles; Performa 13, New York; Acre Projects, Chicago; Chinati Foundation, Marfa; the Neuberger Museum of Art, Purchase, NY; Shin Museum of Art, South Korea; Vox Populi, Philadelphia; and Socrates Sculpture Park, New York. Website: http://jesusbenavente.net Instagram: @testotesto3

item.title: The Technology Leadership Advantage Series
item.description:
Tuesday, August 18, 2026 at 12 PM

Location: Ion, 4201 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Register here: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/1995696286315?aff=oddtdtcreator Technology Isn’t Your Competitive Advantage Anymore. Leadership Is. Why High-Growth Companies Win Long Before They Write Another Line of Code Technology has never been more powerful or more accessible. Cloud infrastructure, enterprise software, AI models, development tools, and specialized technical capabilities that once separated companies are now available to almost everyone. Yet companies with access to remarkably similar technology continue to produce very different results. The difference is increasingly leadership. As companies grow, technology decisions stop being purely technical decisions. They become decisions about growth, capital, customers, product direction, risk, organizational design, and competitive position. And the leadership model that helped a company reach one stage of growth may not be the leadership model it needs for the next. Join Ram Prasad, CEO of Delence, for an executive conversation about where competitive advantage is moving and why high-growth companies need to build technology leadership before growth exposes the gap. This isn’t a technical presentation about tools, platforms, or the latest AI trend. It’s a conversation about leadership, growth, technology, and the decisions that shape enterprise value. What We’ll Discuss Why access to technology is becoming less differentiated Why leadership and judgment become more valuable as technology becomes more accessible How growth changes what companies need from technology leadership Why organizations can add engineers, platforms, and tools without improving execution Why companies sometimes outgrow the leadership model that got them here Why AI creates an executive leadership challenge, not simply a technology opportunity How strong technology leadership connects business strategy, product, technology, AI, and execution How to recognize leadership gaps before they become growth constraints Who Should Attend This session is specifically designed for CEOs, seeded startup founders, presidents, investors, private equity leaders, operating partners, and board members of growth-stage B2B technology and technology-enabled companies. It will be particularly relevant if your organization is experiencing rapid growth, increasing technology complexity, product scaling challenges, AI investment, or questions about whether the current leadership structure is ready for the next stage. If technology decisions are increasingly becoming CEO, board, investment, or growth decisions, this conversation is for you. One Question to Consider Before You Arrive Is your leadership team built for the next three years and not the last three? About Ram Prasad Ram Prasad is CEO of Delence and an executive technology leader focused on the intersection of technology, product, AI, and business growth. Throughout his corporate career, Ram has worked with executive teams navigating the decisions that emerge as organizations grow when technology becomes more complex, product priorities compete, AI creates new possibilities, and decisions that were once technical begin affecting growth, risk, and enterprise value. His perspective is built around a simple idea: Growth has a leadership problem. Ram speaks and advises on executive technology leadership, AI strategy, product strategy, scaling, and the leadership decisions that turn technology into business advantage. About Delence Delence provides executive technology leadership to growth-stage B2B technology and technology-enabled companies. Through Fractional CAIO, CTO and CPO leadership, Delence works alongside CEOs and executive teams when the business needs senior technology, product, or AI leadership, but a permanent executive hire may not yet be the right answer. Delence connects business strategy, technology, product, AI, and execution, bringing executive ownership to the decisions that become more consequential as companies grow. This isn’t staffing or recruiting. It is executive leadership for the stage the business is entering.

item.title: Mapping Houston's Innovation Ecosystem
item.description:
Friday, August 21, 2026 at 10 AM

Location: Ion – Conference Room 027, 4201 Main St, Houston, TX, 77002

Facilitated by Wade Pinder, Ion’s Mentor in Residence Houston’s startup and innovation ecosystem is as vast and dynamic as the city itself, full of opportunities, resources, and talent. Yet, navigating it can be challenging—especially for those unfamiliar with its many parts. Whether you’re an entrepreneur, investor, educator, student, community leader or curious professional, this session will offer valuable insights into how Houston’s innovation ecosystem works and how you can find your place within it. Discover the Houston Ecosystem’s Flow Facilitated by Wade Pinder, the Ion’s Mentor in Residence, this session will help participants map out the journey needed to take an idea from concept to a mature company. Wade brings years of experience in product management, community building, and mentoring entrepreneurs to the table, offering a thoughtful and informed perspective to guide this exploration. The heart of the session lies in exploring a dynamic mind map that Wade has created and continues to refine—an ever-evolving, community-driven tool that grows alongside Houston’s innovation ecosystem. Attendees will not only learn about the ecosystem’s flow but also have the opportunity to contribute to it by identifying gaps, sharing knowledge, and adding their insights. This session will center on the stages of a company’s growth journey, exploring the essential elements that drive it forward. Participants will examine the role of financial capital, from early fundraising efforts to securing the resources needed for scaling, and how these milestones align with a company’s progression. The discussion will also delve into the human element of growing a business, highlighting the evolving talent and expertise required to navigate the entrepreneurial journey. Additionally, we’ll explore the importance of “social capital”—the networks, support systems, and relationships that play a critical role in moving ideas to market and sustaining long-term growth. Ion’s Vision Helping the community better understand the local ecosystem reflects the Ion’s commitment “to being the home for Houston’s innovation community.” By fostering connections, creating opportunities, and sharing perspectives, the Ion is building a transformative culture that strengthens Houston’s economic resiliency and celebrates the entrepreneurial journey. From forming an initial entrepreneurial idea to the prototyping phase to scaling a business, this Houston Ecosystem Mapping session aligns with the Ion’s goals to support innovation, attract talent, and build a vibrant ecosystem. Who Should Attend? This session is ideal for: Entrepreneurs looking to understand greater Houston’s resources. Investors curious about the local startup landscape. Professionals and students wanting to connect with the innovation community. Anyone passionate about Houston’s growth as a hub for innovation and entrepreneurship. Innovators who have recently moved to greater Houston and are looking to get “plugged in” to the local scene. Community leaders and service providers that support (or want to support) the innovation ecosystem. Register today for this chance to explore Houston’s ecosystem, uncover its flow, and help shape its future.

item.title: OVERFLOW RADIO: Šakotayišol Nunuš Constellation
item.description:
Saturday, October 3, 2026 at 12 AM

Location: DiverseWorks – Gallery @ MATCH, 3400 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

October 3-24, 2026DiverseWorks Gallery @ MATCHGallery Hours: 12 noon – 6 pm, Thursday-Saturday Celebrated for her large-scale social choreographies, Emily Johnson / Catalyst’s newest project, Overflow Radio is a performance, skill-share, planting of 1000 trees, and radio transmission from across territories. In conjunction with the world premiere of Overflow Radio in Mni Sóta Makoce (Minneapolis), DiverseWorks hosts an Overflow Radio: Šakotayišol Nunuš Constellation here in Houston. Over 24 non-consecutive hours, we will gather in-person to listen to twelve First Nations and Indigenous authors, poets, and scholars live-broadcasting from their home territories and First Nations. We’ll pay attention to other scales, other forms, other knowledges. We’ll traverse together, transcending colonial borders, languages and time. We’ll feast and celebrate the making of community, as we practice our shared commitment to creating our possible futures, as we gather what we need to know. The program is developed in collaboration with Emily Johnson and local Indigenous and Native artists to include talks, skill-shares, listening gatherings, an exhibition, and performances by Aveda Adara, Chiara Beaumont, Chichi, Karen Navarro, Aryn Ward and Monica Villarreal, with additional participating artists and community partners to be announced. The project is co-organized by DiverseWorks, Emily Johnson / Catalyst, and the participating artists and partners. Programs (please check back for updated information)DW Art + Climate CONVERSATIONS: Emily Johnson, 6:30 pm July 29Opening Event and Reception: 5 – 8 pm, October 3Listening Gatherings: 12noon – 6 pm (specific hours TBD), October 9-12Diverse Discourse Lecture & Studio Visits: Mary Bourdeaux: October 16-19 / Lecture 6 pm, Oct. 17 AcknowledgementsOverflow Radio is a National Performance Network Creation & Development Fund Project commissioned by Roy and Edna Disney / CalArts Theater (REDCAT) and co-commissioned DiverseWorks, MASS MoCA and University of Minnesota Department of Theatre Arts & Dance, more information at www.npnweb.org. Overflow Radio is developed through creative residencies provided by MASS MoCA, John and Mabel Ringling Museum of Art, Roy and Edna Disney / CalArts Theater, University of Minnesota’s Imagine Fund with support from the McKnight Foundation, and Danspace Project with support from the New York State DanceForce, a partnership program of the New York State Council on the Arts. Overflow Radio is created with generous support from First Peoples Fund, Howard Gilman Foundation, Harkness Foundation for Dance, and the New England Foundation for the Arts’ National Dance Project with lead funding from the Doris Duke Foundation and The Mellon Foundation.
